title: CoSaNN designs and tests an induced-fit carbohydrate kinase
summary: CoSaNN combined neural structure prediction, learned sequence optimization and solubility ranking to design variants of an induced-fit ROK carbohydrate kinase. The authors measured expression, thermal stability and activity in vitro. The paper reports measurable expression for 189 of 348 designs in one table, while the strategy-level counts do not sum to that total; no success-rate claim is made here.
ai_technology: CoSaNN: AlphaFold2-based conformation modeling, ProteinMPNN sequence design and SolvIT graph neural network ranking

source_review.scope: Primary PMC full text and PNAS DOI record for CoSaNN-guided glucokinase design, Enzymit affiliations, experimental activity results and the discrepancy in reported design totals.

evidence.tested: The authors applied CoSaNN to redesign the Arthrobacter polyphosphate glucokinase ROK kinase and performed expression, thermal-stability and enzyme-activity assays on designed variants. The primary Results table reports 189 designs with detectable soluble expression among 348 listed designs; its strategy counts (119+95+94 plus 40 in another strategy; rows in the prose/table are internally inconsistent) do not reconcile cleanly, so the record does not use a single total as a success-rate denominator.
evidence.unknown: The study tests a company-designed enzyme set in vitro; it does not establish industrial deployment. The primary paper’s count inconsistency remains explicitly disclosed.
evidence.ai_role: CoSaNN uses deep-learning structure prediction (AlphaFold2), sequence optimization with ProteinMPNN and a learned solubility classifier (SolvIT) to rank enzyme designs for experimental characterization.
